accuracy.evidence: Checked against NHM London and AMNH pages: pterosaurs (Pteranodon) were flying reptiles and plesiosaurs and ichthyosaurs were marine reptiles, close relatives but not dinosaurs; Dimetrodon (about 295-272 million years ago) predates dinosaurs and is a synapsid with a sprawling gait; non-bird dinosaurs died out 66 million years ago, Homo sapiens appeared about 300,000 years ago and overlapped with woolly mammoths; Stegosaurus lived about 155-150 million years ago; T. rex had two-fingered short arms; Velociraptor was about turkey-sized with quill knobs (Turner et al. 2007). The three checks are stated as necessary conditions only ('if it fails one, it is not a dinosaur'), and the adult notes say scientists define dinosaurs by family tree and bones and count birds as living dinosaurs, so the simplification is not wrong.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented confusions in museum education material: every big or prehistoric animal is a dinosaur (Pteranodon, plesiosaurs, Dimetrodon and mammoths are the classic examples), people lived alongside dinosaurs (cartoon cavemen), and films are accurate (the person-sized scaly Velociraptor). Each appears in the scene, the time line, the film sort, the checks and the challenge.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is about this topic's own question, what counts as a dinosaur: a sky/land/sea scene where only the non-dinosaurs are targets, a front-view leg-stance manipulation contrasting a lizard's sprawl with an upright dinosaur, a time order that puts Dimetrodon before and people after the dinosaurs, a film-or-fossil sort and a three-question check. The gate measures it under 30% similar to every flagship lab, including flagdino and flagdinosize, which teach fossils as evidence and size comparison.

lab_teaches.evidence: Tapping a real dinosaur in the scene tells the child it is a dinosaur and why, so the 'not a dinosaur' reasons (flies with skin wings, swims with flippers, has fur) are discovered one by one; dragging the feet in lifts the body high, showing what 'legs under the body' means; a wrong time slot names who came before or after; the final check applies the same three tests to new animals, including one that passes.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: 'Yes, a flying dinosaur' for Pteranodon (the scene marks it a flying reptile), 'Legs out to the side' (only the lizard stands that way; the dinosaur's legs go under the body) and 'Yes, long ago' for people seeing a T. rex (the time line puts people last, long after T. rex). The done message names what the child predicted.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with answers in rotating positions; every wrong option has a slip tag with its own message: 'fly' (pterosaurs were flying reptile cousins), 'sea' (sea reptiles with flippers were not dinosaurs), 'old' (living long ago does not make a dinosaur), 'big' (some dinosaurs were chicken-sized), 'time' (dinosaurs died out 66 million years ago, people came much later), 'film' (films are made up; fossils tell us) and 'legs' (lizard sprawl versus legs under the body).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the readability limits (kid at most 6.5, adult at most 9.5). Kid sentences are short and concrete ('It was a flying reptile.', 'Their legs went straight down under the body, like the legs of a table.'). Canvas prompts are one line, scene labels name Sky, Land and Sea, and every animal is a picture as well as a name for ages 5-7.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one idea: where and how dinosaurs stood; which animals of long ago were not dinosaurs and why; people never met the big dinosaurs; films versus fossils. Adult paragraphs give the curriculum links and key words, the three checks and their limits, the named mistakes, and what the lab does. The filler gate passes.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark and at desktop for every step before and after Show me. Fixes made from screenshots: the dinosaur's sprawled right foot was clipped at the canvas edge and overlapped the lizard (figure now smaller and shifted), the time-line card names were cut off ('Dimetro', 'mammo'; the picture is now smaller and the font fits each word), the plesiosaur was hard to see on the dark-theme sea (darker animal, brighter sea), and the legs step had an empty top (now carries a one-line instruction). Animals in the scene are about 90 px tap targets; Yes/No pills are 52 px tall.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin with a descriptive aria-label ('Pteranodon: mark it as not a dinosaur', 'Put the left leg straight under the body', 'Put T. rex in place 2nd', 'Some dinosaurs had feathers: Real', 'Stegosaurus: Did it walk on land? Yes'); the canvas aria-label is updated live with each reply; the challenge uses real buttons and a polite live region; axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and phone in the browser gate.
